verdict.line: You lose if you let Fiora stack Duelist for free with Riposte up; you win if you force Death's Grasp through and lock in Realm of Death.

brief.thesis: This is an even lane at 47.2% over 2078 games because Fiora's Riposte punishes committed cooldowns while Mordekaiser's sustained magic damage and shield from Indestructible out-value her in a drawn-out fight. The matchup is decided by whether you bait out her parry before you commit E (Death's Grasp) or R (Realm of Death), not by raw stats.

theirWindow.when: Riposte is up and you're in E range
theirWindow.what: She can parry Death's Grasp or Realm of Death entirely, negating your engage and healing off the block via Duelist stacks. Throw a Q (Obliterate) first to bait it or wait the 10-6s cooldown out.

yourWindow.what: This is your window to land E (Death's Grasp) and immediately follow with R (Realm of Death). Once you've pulled her in, she can't escape the duel and your W (Indestructible) shield will keep stacking off her Lunge damage.

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: Taken in 67.8% of games (48.1% win rate over 1708 games); the extra sustain from two potions outlasts her Lunge poke until your first back.

boots.why: Picked in 86.1% of games for a reason — the flat damage reduction blunts her auto-reliant Duelist stacking and her double-Lunge burst.

core.why: The slow from your Q and E lets you keep her inside Death's Grasp range instead of letting her kite with Burst of Speed.
Omnivamp sustains you through extended trades where her Duelist passive is also healing her — you need to out-heal, not just out-damage.
Core pick in 6.1% of this build path; the grievous wounds shuts down her Duelist healing entirely once she's committed to the fight.

situational.when: she rushes crit items or you're getting outpaced by her R (Blade Waltz) burst
she builds tank or the game goes long and you need more sustained DPS over Thornmail's utility
you need the extra ability haste to shorten your E and R cooldowns for repeat engages

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustained stacking damage rewards you for staying in extended trades, which is exactly where Mordekaiser beats Fiora once her all-in windows pass.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport runs a 48.8% win rate (11.5% pick) and lets you reset after level 6 all-ins without losing CS lead, which matters since this matchup is decided by repeated skirmishes rather than one early kill window.

playing.title: Bait Riposte with Q first
playing.detail: Throw Obliterate before committing E (Death's Grasp) — if she parries the Q instead of your E, her Riposte is wasted and your engage is now safe for its full 16-8s cooldown window.

playing.title: Track her Lunge charge count
playing.detail: Lunge can be used twice within a couple seconds at no mana cost — if she's already used one dash, the second is still live and will close distance on your retreat.

playing.title: Don't R into an up Riposte
playing.detail: Realm of Death locks you both in; if she still has Riposte available when you cast it, she can parry inside the pocket dimension and you get nothing for your 140-80s cooldown ultimate.

playing.title: Stack Darkness Rise before trading
playing.detail: Land 3 spells or attacks on her first to trigger your passive's damage aura and move speed — this flips short trades in your favor even without full combo access.

playing.title: Hold W shield for her all-in, not chip damage
playing.detail: Indestructible stores damage dealt and taken — pop it to heal only after she's committed Burst of Speed and Lunge, not on early poke.

playing.title: Respect her E move speed stacking
playing.detail: Burst of Speed grants move speed per attack or Lunge landed during its duration — once she's chained three hits, she can outrun your slow-free kit; disengage before that stacks up.

playing.title: Push waves before her double reset
playing.detail: Killing a champion refreshes her Burst of Speed cooldown entirely — avoid giving her a kill under tower, since it resets her engage tool for free.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win-rate figures are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the cooldown numbers, ability mechanics, and tactical sequencing above are my own reading of the kit interactions, not measured data.
